sections.html:
Kaysville is a city in Davis County, Utah, and it is part of the Ogden-Clearfield metropolitan area. Layton lies to the north, Fruit Heights to the east, and Farmington, the county seat, to the south.

The city covers 10.54 square miles at an elevation of roughly 4,298 feet, in a county that lies between the Great Salt Lake on the west and the Wasatch Range on the east. That inhabited strip of land is known as the Wasatch Front.

With only 2.4% of homes vacant in 2020, Kaysville has very few empty houses. A vacant or neglected property stands out on a street where nearly every neighbor lives next door year-round.

sections.h2: How did Kaysville get its name and its start?
sections.html:
Kaysville was settled in 1847 by Hector Haight, who was sent north to find feed for livestock, and it is named for William Kay, appointed bishop of the local ward in 1851. Samuel Holmes built a cabin about two miles north in 1849, and Edward Phillips and John Green joined him after heavy snow stopped their trip toward Ogden.

The settlement was first called Kay's Ward. Residents once asked to rename it Freedom, and the city's history page records Brigham Young's reply: 'When did Kay's Ward get its Freedom.' The name stayed. Kaysville was incorporated on March 15, 1868, as the first city in Davis County and the 27th in Utah Territory.

A fort of about 15 square blocks was laid out in 1854, though only the south and west walls were finished, and it came down around 1870. On December 18, 1977, United Airlines Flight 2860 crashed near Kaysville.

sections.h2: What do Kaysville residents do for work, and what does it mean for selling?
sections.html:
Davis County is often described as a bedroom community, with many residents commuting to Salt Lake County. Hill Air Force Base, in the northern part of the county, is the largest employer, with nearly 23,000 military and civilian personnel, and it accounts for about 12% of the county economy.

Other major county employers are the Davis School District, Lagoon Amusement Park and Lifetime Products. Owners whose jobs depend on these employers or on a Salt Lake County commute may have a work-driven reason to move, and a sale with a fixed closing date can help them plan.

  • Anyone relocating for work can ask a buyer to confirm a closing date in writing.
  • A house that has to be vacated before a move can be sold as it stands, without staging.
  • Heirs who live out of state can handle a sale through a title company without being in Kaysville.

sections.h2: Which schools and city services serve Kaysville?
sections.html:
Davis School District, whose boundaries match the county's, serves Kaysville, and Davis High School is the city's high school. Wikipedia's district list counts 16 schools in Kaysville: nine elementary, three junior high, one high school and three special schools.

The city's own services page lists garbage, curbside recycling, green waste recycling, power, pressure irrigation, storm water and water. Sewer also appears on that list, but it is supplied by Central Davis Sewer rather than the city itself. Kaysville City Power is at 721 W Old Mill Lane and can be reached at 801-544-8925.

sections.h2: What does the city charge for building permits, and why should sellers care?
sections.html:
Kaysville bases permit fees on project value, adds a 1% state education fee and a 25% plan check fee, and posts a fee schedule online. The city also lists impact fees for a new single-family home, and a few of them appear below.

ItemKaysville fee
Parks and recreation impact fee, new home$4,480
Central Davis Sewer fee, new home$2,400
North Davis Sewer fee, new home$3,454.03
Basement finish or remodel permit$245.70
Furnace, A/C or water heater permit$65.65

Permits expire if work has not started within 180 days or stops for 180 days, and the construction bond is forfeited when that happens. A seller with a half-finished basement and an expired permit may find that a lender-backed buyer asks for it to be closed out first. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands and deal with the permit afterward.

sections.h2: Can I rent out part of my Kaysville house?
sections.html:
Kaysville allows internal accessory dwelling units, but the owner must live in either the main home or the unit as a primary residence. The rules are in Kaysville City Code 17-31-3.

  • If someone who is not a related family member will live in the unit, the city requires a permit.
  • The unit needs its own paved parking space, in addition to the two-car garage and two-car driveway.
  • Detached structures, such as an apartment over a garage or a granny flat, cannot be used as a dwelling.
  • Additions or remodels done to create the unit need a building permit.

Sellers who bought a Kaysville house with a basement apartment should confirm that the apartment was set up under these rules. Because the owner must occupy the property, a house that is rented in full with an apartment inside may not qualify.

sections.h2: What are the property tax steps for a Kaysville home?
sections.html:
Davis County sends valuation notices at the end of July, and the 2026 appeal deadline is September 15 according to the county, though one section of its instructions says September 16, so owners should confirm the date before filing. State law sets the deadline as the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor provides the notice.

Only market value can be appealed, not the tax rate. The Davis County Commission serves as the Board of Equalization, and it relies on recommendations from hearing officers it appoints. Evidence can include closing documents, a certified appraisal or comparable sales, and an agent filing for an owner needs a notarized authorization.

  • Tax Administration is at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington.
  • Phone: 801-451-3331 or 801-451-3329.
  • Late appeals go to the Board of Equalization, which may accept them for extenuating circumstances.

Under Utah's primary residential exemption, a qualifying home is taxed on 55% of market value. After a sale, the new owner has to submit a new application, so a seller should tell the buyer to expect that step.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Kaysville house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Kaysville closes at a title company, and the deed is recorded with the Davis County Recorder. Because no loan is involved, the steps are a purchase contract, a title search, signatures on a settlement statement and the recording of the deed.

Utah law requires a deed that conveys title to name the grantees, list a mailing address for assessment and taxation, and include a legal description that meets state standards. A county recorder may also ask for the tax identification number on the instrument.

When a house sells mid-year, the title company normally prorates the year's tax at closing. Ask for the proration figure before the closing date.

sections.h2: What do Kaysville sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Kaysville is a family-heavy city, with a median age of 29.9 and 52.4% of households raising children under 18, so a house that stands empty after an owner moves or passes away can sit out of step with its street. Carrying costs keep running while it waits.

  • Inherited houses that need updating before a conventional listing.
  • Basement apartments that were set up without a permit or without the required parking space.
  • Expired building permits with a forfeited bond.
  • Owners who must relocate and cannot manage showings from afar.

Whichever route a seller picks, compare the net amount after repairs, commission and carrying costs, and read any contract before signing.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Davis County?
faqs.a: The county lists September 15, 2026 for the 2026 tax year, though one part of its instructions says September 16. State law uses the later of September 15 or 45 days after the notice, so confirm with Tax Administration at 801-451-3331 before filing.

faqs.q: Can I put an apartment in my Kaysville basement?
faqs.a: Yes, as an internal accessory dwelling unit, if you live in the main home or the unit. It needs its own paved parking space, and a permit is required if a non-family member will live there.

faqs.q: Who provides sewer service in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Central Davis Sewer provides sewer service, not the city. The city provides water, power, pressure irrigation, garbage, recycling and storm water.

faqs.q: Do building permits expire in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Yes. A permit expires if work does not start within 180 days of issuance or stops for 180 days. The bond is then forfeited and a new application is needed.

faqs.q: How many people live in Kaysville?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 32,945 residents in 2020, and its estimate for July 1, 2025 is 33,307.
